policies.title: Named ordinary passports: advance Dominican tourist visa
policies.summary: DGII expressly says tourists from these named countries cannot enter with a Tourist Card and must obtain a visa at a Dominican diplomatic mission. The MIREX service describes the corresponding consular tourist-visa route.
conditions: This is the ordinary-passport tourist baseline only. DGII says the named nationalities must request a visa at a Dominican diplomatic mission; MIREX describes a consular tourism visa, not an eVisa or visa on arrival.

MIREX states that Decree 691-07 lets a traveller with permanent residence or a valid multiple-entry visa for the United States, Schengen/EU area, Canada, or the United Kingdom enter for tourism with a Tourist Card. That third-country-document exception does not make any listed passport nationality unconditionally visa-free.

The consular tourism visa is stated as 60 days and one entry, or 60 days and two entries for the multiple variant; applications, passport validity, financial evidence, purpose, security screening and final admission remain required.

Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Montenegro and Papua New Guinea are excluded because the live MIREX ordinary-passport selector contradicts this DGII list without a reconciled current instrument. Mongolia and Morocco are excluded because separately documented ordinary-passport visa waivers control.
This policy does not establish work, business, study, residence, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, border-card, refugee, stateless, emergency, or other special-document treatment.

application.label: Dominican Republic consular tourist visa service
application.processingTime: MIREX states a 10-to-20-business-day response time for the visa service.
steps: Contact the Dominican embassy or consulate serving the applicant's residence or designated jurisdiction.
Submit the tourism-visa application, valid passport and the stated supporting evidence to the competent consular service.
Travel only after the visa is issued and complete the separate DGM e-Ticket declaration.

policies.title: Other ordinary passports: Tourist Card without consular visa
policies.summary: DGII expressly provides that nationals not in its named visa-required list enter with a Tourist Card. The card permits tourism without a consular visa; it is an entry tax/formality, not an ETA or visa on arrival.
conditions: Tourist purposes only; DGII states the Tourist Card gives a maximum 30-day stay, with extension administered by DGM. A person who undertakes lucrative activity loses its use and must hold the suitable visa.

The Tourist Card is a US$10 entry tax/formality, included in airline tickets issued outside the Dominican Republic for air arrivals; it may be purchased at land or sea points. It is not an electronic travel authorization, eVisa, or a visa issued at the border.

The DGM e-Ticket is a separate mandatory online entry-and-exit declaration for every passenger, not an ETA or visa. Passport validity, return/onward travel, border screening and admission remain applicable.

HK and MO represent only the ordinary Hong Kong SAR and Macao SAR passport routes respectively; this policy does not establish a route for other PRC, SAR, diplomatic, official, service or special travel documents.

South Sudan is excluded because the DGII residual rule conflicts with the live MIREX ordinary-passport selector. Latvia, Romania and Samoa are separately excluded because the DGII named list and live MIREX selector conflict. This policy does not establish citizenship, residence, business, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, border-card, refugee, stateless, emergency or other special-document treatment.

policies.title: Mongolian ordinary passports: bilateral visa waiver
policies.summary: The current MIREX ordinary-tourist selector says Mongolian ordinary passports do not require a visa and that the measure has been in force since 10 June 2026. The Dominican Constitutional Court reproduces the underlying bilateral agreement, which waives visas for valid ordinary passports for stays of up to 90 days.
conditions: Applies to a valid ordinary Mongolian passport for entry, stay, departure or transit for no more than 90 days from entry under the bilateral agreement.
A stay exceeding 90 days requires a visa in advance. Purpose-specific immigration, passport-validity, transport-carrier, security screening and final-admission requirements remain separate.

DGII’s Tourist Card list continues to name Mongolia as visa-required. The targeted current MIREX ordinary-passport tourist result and the agreement’s reproduced ordinary-passport scope are preferred for this direct conflict; recheck operational guidance if either authority changes it.
This policy does not establish residence, work, study, crew, diplomatic, official, service, special-document or individual-admissibility treatment.

policies.title: Moroccan ordinary passports: bilateral tourism/business visa waiver
policies.summary: MIREX records the Dominican Republic–Morocco tourism and business visa-exemption agreement as in force from 14 July 2021. This later treaty route prevails over Morocco’s continued appearance on the DGII tourist-card visa list.
conditions: Applies to the agreement’s tourism and business waiver scope for ordinary Moroccan passports, according to the live MIREX treaty registry and ordinary-passport tourist selector.

The reviewed registry does not state a stay limit, activity conditions beyond the treaty title, document rules, or admission requirements; these remain subject to the agreement and Dominican immigration controls.

DGII’s current Tourist Card page still lists Morocco among nationalities requiring a consular visa. The in-force MIREX treaty record and selector are preferred for this direct treaty conflict; operational recheck remains warranted.
This policy does not establish residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, service, special-document or individual-admissibility treatment.

conflicts.explanation: The current MIREX ordinary-tourist selector says no visa and states that the measure has been in force since 10 June 2026. The Dominican Constitutional Court reproduces the bilateral agreement, which waives visas for valid ordinary passports for stays up to 90 days.

unresolved.reason: The reviewed tourist-card and foreigner visa sources do not directly establish a Dominican ordinary-passport holder's right-of-entry classification. The e-Ticket applies to all passengers but is not an entry authorization.
